title: ticfac devex: one command to run, watch and triage an epic, locally and in the cloud
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-26: 'i want to make devex / agentex super smooth on that local execution scenario, it seems a bit convoluted now, when i look at the commands (that comment could apply to cloud as well)'. Widened from the original scope ('a skill system and a one-line install, mirroring tk', 2026-09-15), which stays in.

THE FRICTION TODAY, running one local epic on claude in herdr panes:
  GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) nohup ticfac run-epic -profiles ~/Development/ticfac/profiles-herdr -wall 86400 gvc > log &
  then ticfac status epic-gvc / ticfac events epic-gvc --follow / ticfac findings gvc / ticfac finding --promote-as X --by 'who' gvc <64-hex key>
A token the tool could fetch itself; a filesystem path to a profile set; a wall clock whose default is wrong; a run id that is not the epic id; backgrounding by hand; three commands to follow one run; 64-hex keys typed by hand to triage. The operator's orchestrating agent papers over all of it with hand-rolled watchers and polling loops, which is the clearest sign the tool should do it.

THE SHAPE:
- ticfac run <epic>: starts in the background and attaches the live view; running it again resumes. It takes the epic id everywhere. It fetches the GitHub token from gh when (and only when) the repo's close-out needs a forge. It detects herdr and dispatches into panes by default (--no-herdr opts out), using EMBEDDED profile sets, never a path. There is no wall-clock default; liveness is b1t's.
- ticfac (no args): every run on this machine and the factory, attention first. Every stop screen names the reason and the one command that clears it.
- ticfac init: writes .tick/runners.toml (+ .local/.cloud) and .tick/config.md from a few questions (local/cloud, claude/pi), with the gate guessed from the repo; ticfac doctor checks herdr, gh, tk, and docker/wrangler for cloud.
- ticfac triage <epic>: walks each untriaged finding (absorb / file / fixed / discard) interactively, and with --json for agents; short key prefixes accepted.
- Agent experience: --json on every command, stable exit codes (held-for-person, failed, done and running are distinguishable without parsing prose), and a ticfac skill (installed like tk's) that teaches the loop in about twenty lines. The ticks skill owns planning and tick shape; the ticfac skill owns execution; they must not contradict each other.
- Cloud parity: ticfac run <epic> --cloud, with the same view, verbs and triage.
- Distribution: goreleaser + install.sh behind a stable URL, as ticks ships.
Built on cobra + fang (nwj), a versioned status model (6dh) and the in-place watch (89m) already planned here.
acceptance_criteria:
[A1] On a repo with tk and herdr, 'ticfac init' then 'ticfac run <epic>' runs an epic on claude in herdr panes with no other flag, env var or path, and 'ticfac run <epic>' again resumes it.
[A2] 'ticfac' with no arguments shows every local and cloud run, attention first, and every stop names its reason and the one command that clears it.
[A3] 'ticfac triage <epic>' settles every untriaged finding without typing a 64-hex key.
[A4] Every command has --json and a documented stable exit code set; an agent can start, follow, triage and finish an epic from the ticfac skill alone.
[A5] 'ticfac run <epic> --cloud' uses the same verbs, view and triage as a local run.
[A6] A user who has never built ticfac installs the binary with one command and the skill the way they install the ticks skill; the two skills state their boundary and do not contradict each other.
